Bayraktar is partially supported by the National Science Foundation under grant DMS-2106556 and by the Susan M. Smith chair. Y. Dolinsky is supported in part by the GIF Grant 1489-304.6/
arxiv-2107-01568.creator: Erhan Bayraktar, Christoph Czichowsky, Leonid Dolinskyi, Yan Dolinsky
arxiv-2107-01568.description: Abstract . The aim of this short note is to establish a limit theorem for the optimal trading strategies in the setup of the utility maximization problem with proportional transaction costs. This limit theorem resolves the open question from [ 4 ] . The main idea of our proof is to establish a uniqueness result for the optimal strategy.

arxiv-2207-12332.title: Four New Fast Radio Bursts Discovered in the Parkes 70-cm Pulsar Survey Archive 2022 Four New Fast Radio Bursts Discovered in the Parkes 70-cm Pulsar Survey Archive – References
arxiv-2207-12332.creator: F. Crawford, S. Hisano, M. Golden, T. Kikunaga, A. Laity, D. Zoeller
arxiv-2207-12332.description: Abstract We present four new fast radio bursts discovered in a search of the Parkes 70-cm pulsar survey data archive for dispersed single pulses and bursts. We searched dispersion measures (DMs) ranging between 0 to 5000 pc cm -3 with the HEIMDALL and FETCH detection and classification algorithms.

arxiv-2302-04313.title: Geometry-Complete Diffusion for 3D Molecule Generation and Optimization
arxiv-2302-04313.creator: Alex Morehead, Jianlin Cheng
arxiv-2302-04313.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alex Morehead, Jianlin Cheng. Motivation: Generative deep learning methods have recently been proposed for generating 3D molecules using equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs) within a denoising diffusion framework. However, such methods are unable to learn important geometric properties of 3D molecules, as they adopt molecule-agnostic and non-geometric GNNs as their 3D graph denoising networks, which notably hinders their ability to generate valid large 3D molecules.

arxiv-2311-02427.title: Succinct Data Structure for Graphs with d d -Dimensional t t -Representation
arxiv-2311-02427.creator: Girish Balakrishnan ∗, Sankardeep Chakraborty †, Seungbum Jo ‡, N S Narayanaswamy ∗, and Kunihiko Sadakane † ∗ Indian Institute of Technology Madras, † University of Tokyo, Chennai, India Tokyo, Japan girishb@cse.iitm.ac.in sankardeep.chakraborty@gmail.com swamy@cse.iitm.ac.in sada@mist.i.u-tokyo.ac
arxiv-2311-02427.description: Abstract Erdős and West (Discrete Mathematics’85) considered the class of n n vertex intersection graphs which have a d d -dimensional t t -representation , that is, each vertex of a graph in the class has an associated set consisting of at most t t d d -dimensional axis-parallel boxes.

arxiv-2406-01713.title: Walk on Spheres for PDE-based Path Planning
arxiv-2406-01713.creator: Rafael I. Cabral Muchacho, Florian T. Pokorny
arxiv-2406-01713.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the Walk on Spheres algorithm (WoS) for motion planning in robotics. WoS is a Monte Carlo method to solve the Dirichlet problem developed in the 50s by Muller [ 1 ] and has recently been repopularized by Sawhney and Crane [ 2 ] who showed its applicability for geometry processing in volumetric domains.

arxiv-2406-06381.title: Feature Characterization for Profile Surface Texture
arxiv-2406-06381.creator: A Müller, M Eifler, A Jawaid, J Seewig
arxiv-2406-06381.description: Abstract Conventional field parameters for surface measurement use all data points, while feature characterization focuses on subsets extracted by watershed segmentation. This approach enables the extraction of specific features that are potentially responsible for the function of the surface or are a direct reflection of the manufacturing process, allowing for a more accurate assessment of both aspects.

arxiv-2410-01716.title: Exploring Defects with Degrees of Freedom in Free Scalar CFTs
arxiv-2410-01716.creator: Vladimir Bashmakov, Jacopo Sisti
arxiv-2410-01716.description: Abstract Defects in conformal field theories are interesting objects to study from both formal and applied points of view. In this paper, we construct conformal defects in free scalar field CFTs in diverse dimensions. After discussing the possible quadratic defects, we explore interacting setups.

arxiv-2410-15223.title: Moment method and continued fraction expansion in Floquet Operator Krylov Space
arxiv-2410-15223.creator: Hsiu-Chung Yeh, Aditi Mitra
arxiv-2410-15223.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hsiu-Chung Yeh, Aditi Mitra. Recursion methods such as Krylov techniques map complex dynamics to an effective non-interacting problem in one dimension. For example, the operator Krylov space for Floquet dynamics can be mapped to the dynamics of an edge operator of the one-dimensional Floquet inhomogeneous transverse field Ising model (ITFIM), where the latter, after a Jordan-Wigner transformation, is a Floquet model of non-interacting Majorana fermions, and the couplings correspond to Krylov angles.

arxiv-2504-17612.title: Selectively Blind Quantum Computation
arxiv-2504-17612.creator: Abbas Poshtvan, Oleksandra Lapiha, Mina Doosti, Dominik Leichtle, Luka Music, Elham Kashefi
arxiv-2504-17612.description: Abstract Known protocols for the secure delegation of quantum computations from a client to a server in an information-theoretic setting require quantum communication. In this work, we investigate methods to reduce the communication overhead. First, we establish an impossibility result by proving that server-side local processes cannot decrease the quantum communication requirements of secure delegation protocols.

arxiv-2506-15498.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Md Imbesat Hassan Rizvi, Xiaodan Zhu, Iryna Gurevych. Process or step-wise supervision has played a crucial role in advancing complex multi-step reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, efficient, high-quality automated process annotation remains a significant challenge.

arxiv-2509-04095.title: Cloud-Assisted Remote Control for Aerial Robots: From Theory to Proof-of-Concept Implementation
arxiv-2509-04095.creator: Achilleas Santi Seisa, Viswa Narayanan Sankaranarayanan, Gerasimos Damigos, Sumeet Gajanan Satpute, George Nikolakopoulos
arxiv-2509-04095.description: Abstract Cloud robotics has emerged as a promising technology for robotics applications due to its advantages of offloading computationally intensive tasks, facilitating data sharing, and enhancing robot coordination. However, integrating cloud computing with robotics remains a complex challenge due to network latency, security concerns, and the need for efficient resource management.

arxiv-2510-21236.title: Securing AI Agent Execution CCS: Security and privacy Software security engineering CCS: Security and privacy Access control CCS: Computing methodologies Intelligent agents
arxiv-2510-21236.creator: Christoph Bühler, Matteo Biagiola, Luca Di Grazia, Guido Salvaneschi
arxiv-2510-21236.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved into AI agents that interact with external tools and environments to perform complex tasks. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become the de facto standard for connecting agents with such resources, but security has lagged behind: thousands of MCP servers execute with unrestricted access to host systems, creating a broad attack surface.

arxiv-2601-15630.title: Agentic AI Governance and Lifecycle Management in Healthcare
arxiv-2601-15630.creator: Chandra Prakash, Mary Lind, Avneesh Sisodia
arxiv-2601-15630.description: Abstract Healthcare organizations are beginning to embed agentic AI into routine workflows, including clinical documentation support and early-warning monitoring. As these capabilities diffuse across departments and vendors, health systems face agent sprawl causing duplicated agents, unclear accountability, inconsistent controls, and tool permissions that persist beyond the original use case.

pmc-10516208.title: Medical Interns’ Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Toward People Living with HIV: Multicenter Experience from Saudi Arabia
pmc-10516208.creator: Israa Abdullah Malli, Dalia Hamdan, Alhanoof Aljahdali, Amal Almutairi, Raghad Jar, Reham Alzahrani, Muhammad Anwar Khan
pmc-10516208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundDiscrimination by some healthcare providers toward people living with HIV/AIDS has been documented. Differences in cultural backgrounds make it harder for future doctors, who need a lot of knowledge and a positive attitude to treat patients.

pmc-10573252.title: Articular Cartilage—From Basic Science Structural Imaging to Non-Invasive Clinical Quantitative Molecular Functional Information for AI Classification and Prediction
pmc-10573252.creator: Bodo Kurz, Thomas Lange, Marita Voelker, Melanie L Hart, Bernd Rolauffs, Rafal Kamiński
pmc-10573252.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This review presents the changes that the imaging of articular cartilage has undergone throughout the last decades. It highlights that the expectation is no longer to image the structure and associated functions of articular cartilage but, instead, to devise methods for generating non-invasive, function-depicting images with quantitative information that is useful for detecting the early, pre-clinical stage of diseases such as primary or post-traumatic osteoarthritis (OA/PTOA).

pmc-10575166.title: A High-Generalizability Machine Learning Framework for Analyzing the Homogenized Properties of Short Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Composites
pmc-10575166.creator: Yunmei Zhao, Zhenyue Chen, Xiaobin Jian, Alexander S Novikov
pmc-10575166.description: This study aims to develop a high-generalizability machine learning framework for predicting the homogenized mechanical properties of short fiber-reinforced polymer composites. The ensemble machine learning model (EML) employs a stacking algorithm using three base models of Extra Trees (ET), eXtreme Gradient Boosting machine (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting machine (LGBM).

pmc-10725705.title: Parents' Awareness, Knowledge, and Perception of Amblyopia in Children: A Study in Jazan Region, Saudi Arabia
pmc-10725705.creator: Ismail I Abuallut, Khalid M Alameer, Bandar M Abuageelah, Eman Hurissi, Masoud M Alqahtani, Ibrahim M Gosadi, Faisal M Tubaigy, Yousef M Alyami
pmc-10725705.description: BackgroundAmblyopia is a vision disorder that results from a development problem in the brain rather than a neurological disease in the eye. The condition causes reduced visual acuity in one or both eyes due to the brain's inability to process inputs, rather than a structural abnormality.

pmc-11676268.title: Embryonic Development and Cranial Ossification Sequence in Two Heremites Species (Squamata: Scincidae)
pmc-11676268.creator: Kamil Candan, Elif Yıldırım Caynak, Kübra Oğur, Ecem Büşra Hastürk, Ahmet Gökay Korkmaz, Çetin Ilgaz, Serkan Gül, Yusuf Kumlutaş
pmc-11676268.description: Although embryological studies of squamates have a long history, most groups in this large clade remain poorly studied. One such group is the family Scincidae, which consists of morphologically and ecologically diverse lizards. In this study, we describe several stages of embryonic development based on cleared and stained specimens of Heremites auratus and Heremites vittatus.

pmc-12661340.title: Exploring the pharmacokinetic interactions between cisplatin and Triphala through in-vitro, in-vivo, and in-silico approaches – A pilot study to bridge modern medicine with Ayurveda
pmc-12661340.creator: T.K. Girija Kumari, Kamatchi Sundara Saravanan, Lakshmi M. Sundar, Gouri Nair, G.N.S. Hemasree, Ganesan Rajalekshmi Saraswathy
pmc-12661340.description: BackgroundHerbal drugs are often used alongside conventional cancer therapies to mitigate the adverse effects and enhance therapeutic efficacy. Triphala, a traditional herbal formulation used in Ayurveda, is known for its anticancer and CYP2E1 inhibitory properties. Cisplatin, although highly effective in cancer treatment, is known to cause significant hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity which are mediated by toxic metabolites formed through CYP2E1 metabolism.

pmc-12870322.title: CYP27A1 suppresses brain metastasis via ferroptosis in lung adenocarcinoma: a six-gene signature predicting the immunotherapy response and clinical outcomes
pmc-12870322.creator: Lu Xu, Liyou Huang, Zihao Liu, Xiaojie Jiang, Linchun Wen
pmc-12870322.description: Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) brain metastasis has limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. This study aimed to identify molecular drivers, construct a prognostic model, and assess immunotherapy response.Methods:We integrated scRNA-seq data from 4 LUAD patients (GSE117570) and bulk RNA-seq data from the TCGA-LUAD cohort. Brain metastasis-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified via Seurat.

pmc-13169528.title: A feasibility randomised controlled trial of Empowered Conversations: training family carers to enhance their relationships and communication with people living with dementia
pmc-13169528.creator: Lydia Morris, Cassie Eastham, Chris Sutton, Yeliz Prior, Yvonne Sylvestre, Gemma Shields, John Keady, Cathy Riley, Mal Walters, Warren Mansell
pmc-13169528.description: BackgroundThe primary objective of this UK-based trial was to investigate the feasibility of conducting a multi-centre randomised controlled evaluation trial of Empowered Conversations (EC). EC is a 6-session group psychosocial intervention for informal (family) care partners of people living with dementia.

pmc-13333587.title: The Circles of Resilience model: exploring how social and structural conditions foster child resilience in the context of ACEs
pmc-13333587.creator: Clare Viglione, Alec Terrana, Tsung-Chin Wu, Xin M. Tu, Elva M. Arredondo, Noe C. Crespo, Pradeep Gidwani, Job Godino, Kyung E. Rhee, Renée Boynton-Jarrett, Borsika A. Rabin, Eric Hekler

pmc-13390171.title: Real-world creatine supplementation: a large-scale cross-sectional study of use, knowledge, and experiences
pmc-13390171.creator: Jocelyn Burridge, Ali Boolani, Ziyang Zhang, Jordan M. Glenn
pmc-13390171.description: BackgroundCreatine is among the most extensively studied dietary supplements in sports nutrition, yet real-world supplementation patterns, knowledge, and outcomes remain poorly characterized. Prior survey research has focused on competitive athletes and younger male samples, even as the evidence base has expanded to support applications in healthy aging, cognition, and female physiology.
